Yes, people do disappear in the war and did disappear in the war, prisoners, civilians, but here we're talking about the disappearance of an individual who was allegedly within the composition of the volunteers, and that's absolutely impossible, that somebody went out there as a volunteer, his name is on all the lists, somebody kills him over there and then nothing is known further, who the person was, who killed him, where the body is. That's quite an impossible situation, and I had to put that to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, when you will testify, if ever you testify, if you want to, you will explain why it is that among volunteers there were no people who disappeared and why that's impossible. This is not the moment to do this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, resume your questions, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: "Not in a single one of these groups organised by us, this Slobodan Milevojevic, known as Topola, go there, although I heard that this man had a group of his own which acted independently in several war theaters. I knew him personally, and I know that before the liberation of Vukovar, he was expelled from the Leva Supoderica Detachment for indiscipline, and for this reason he could never again be sent to a war theatre in the organisation of the Serbian Radical Party."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, how come you say he couldn't go to other war theaters when he arrived in Vocin and was sent back by Radovan Novacic?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, he couldn't go there in the organisation of the Serbian Radical Party, so how he came there, who knows.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In a bus of the Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did the Serbian Radical Party have its own buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It organised buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And whose buses were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know who gave you buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And did these buses go through the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Who had the right to take over buses from various transport organisations and companies? Who could requisition buses from them? Could the Serbian Radical Party do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. It probably could.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Ah-hah.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To reach an agreement to take buses, to transport volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: If you know he came in a bus of the Serbian Radical Party, what group of volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party was in that bus, who was leading that group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were about 40 men in that group.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You're making that up now right here, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not making it up. I'm telling you what I remember. And they were put up in the school in Vocin. They spent one night there, and on

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now you see how I'm being taken by surprise, telling me next week's witnesses and then the Prosecutor has no right to complain for me not being -- not providing him with the material, because I have to use the weekend, to read the documents -- read through the documents that I have been given for these witnesses, and then to see what I have before me, because I wasn't able to do that ever before, because exhibits started being disclosed to me only as of October last year, and much later the transcripts of the testimony in other trials. So you can see how many pages I have to get through every weekend, but I do get through them, let me tell you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We will meet at 9.00 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just tell me how much time I have at my disposal tomorrow, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have used 29 minutes. You have one hour and 31 minutes left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 2nd day of April, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: [Private session] [Confidentiality partially lifted by order of Trial Chamber]
--- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.49 p.m.,
